result.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
result.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) enables multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to scale capacity efficiently, but expert parameters dominate memory even though only a few experts are activated per token: they account for over 90% of model size in modern MoE-MLLMs (e.g., 54 GB out of about 58 GB in BF16 for InternVL3.5-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B). Expert pruning has emerged as an effective compression strategy, but existing methods aggregate importance uniformly across tokens, ignoring that the same expert may serve different roles for vision versus language processing. To address this, we propose MAEP (Modality-Aware Expert Pruning), a training-free framework that decomposes expert importance by modality in a single forward pass. MAEP introduces (1) Delta-H Output ($ΔH$), a redistribution-aware metric measuring the MoE output change when an expert is removed, and (2) low-attention vision tokens as a vision-side pruning signal that is dataset-stable: its expert-importance ranking remains stable across different datasets. Text-side importance serves as a preservation signal while vision-side importance serves as a pruning signal, and experts are ranked globally across layers. Experiments on three MoE-based MLLMs across multimodal and text benchmarks show that MAEP outperforms modality-agnostic baselines on the majority of multimodal benchmarks while remaining competitive on text-only tasks, reducing the BF16 expert weight footprint by about 27 GB (about 47% of total memory) so that the full weight footprint of an approximately 58 GB model fits within a single 40 GB GPU. Code is available at https://github.com/nota-github/MAEP.

AI.brief_summary: 提出无训练的模态感知专家剪枝框架 MAEP，将 MoE-MLLM 中专家重要性按视觉与语言模态分解，用 ΔH 度量移除专家后的输出变化，并以低注意力视觉 token 作为视觉侧剪枝信号，从而压缩专家权重。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按模态分解的专家级贡献归因与「视觉侧信号可作为裁剪依据」的做法，或可供核查 VLM 内部视觉信息究竟由哪些专家承载、是否存在视觉旁路；但论文目标仅为压缩与显存，未涉及 latent 推理状态或推理期计算分配。
